DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Borrowed Thunder

STS-MS8-L3-1400P-MSELA8-MMG-CFI-02 • MS ELA Grade 8 • How Modern Fiction Draws on Myths and Traditional Stories
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
In a Mirror Monologue, you perform a speech as a character from a modern story, then perform it again as the ancient character your story secretly mirrors. Kenji is rehearsing as a new kid at school, and then he will lift the golden mask and give the same speech as the trickster from an old myth. Storytellers have always done this: they borrow the oldest patterns in the world and pour brand new lives into them.
What old story do you think your favorite book or movie secretly mirrors?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Amara doing?
Look at the picture. Explain Amara's action and its purpose using precise language.
2
What is Kenji holding?
Look at the picture. Explain what Kenji holds and why the mirror matters to his rehearsal, using precise language.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Explain the teacher's action and its purpose, using precise language.
4
What room is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Explain what room this is and justify it from the evidence, using precise language.
5
Tell me about the chart on the wall.
Look at the picture. Explain what the chart contains and how the arrows connect the two columns, using precise language.
6
What is Talia wearing?
Look at the picture. Explain what Talia is wearing and what she is doing, using precise language.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: CCSS RL.8.9 — Analyze how a modern work of fiction draws on themes, patterns of events, or character types from myths, traditional stories, or religious works. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
